newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks record new moderate gain at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks record new moderate gain at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks continued their mild-mannered advance at the close Wednesday, with investors now turning their eyes to Thursday's U.S. consumer prices report, dealers said.

"U.S. indicators are dictating the pace of bidding by the private pension funds, which are now cautiously returning to the market as seen in this week's decent turnover," said Emilio Alessandro at brokers Alessandro.
The blue-chip MerVal index added 0.7 percent to close at 734.58, stretching gains so far this week to 1.4 percent.

"If U.S. consumer prices come in tame tomorrow, the bolsa should keep rising because the stage will be set for the Federal Reserve to seriously consider not raising rates Tuesday," another trader said.
U.S. producer prices caught the markets off guard by falling 0.6 percent in April, against forecasts they would stay flat. The Dow, however, gave back most early gains at the close on profit-taking.
The bolsa's floor volume firmed to 27.8 million pesos from 27 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals surged to 126 million pesos from 70.4 million Tuesday.
The broad market index closed up 0.5 percent, with winners beating losers 30 to 17 and 25 issues closing flat.
Top main-tier performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, Banco Frances and foods giant Molinos Rio de la Plata, which jumped 5.4 percent, 4.7 percent and 4.5 percent, respectively.
MerVal losers were led by carmakers Ciadea and Sevel, which shed 3.7 percent and 1.0 percent, respectively, and holding company Comercial del Plata, off 1.3 percent.
